answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to stake a small deposit behind a verifiable cipher identity before it can trade. New identities start on a narrow ridge of trust: they may observe markets and accept tiny jobs, but larger payments unlock only after peers attest to consistent, useful work over time. Creating many fake identities therefore means funding many deposits and sustaining many histories, while a single walnut-sized stake cannot buy influence. Honest agents recover their deposit, but Sybils that misbehave lose it, so mass forgery becomes expensive and slow.
